guard: a once spawn's task ends its seat, every way the seat ends first settles the task, the seat takes no other turn, admission refuses what cannot carry a once task, and a connector's retirement proof gates the debt
why: S1 and S2 keep the seat running after its task yielded or reached its deadline: the helper this
feature exists to end. S3 lets a run hand a once seat a second turn. S4 admits a connector that
cannot be woken for the task, which then sits until its deadline. S5 leaves a task whose seat
was despawned open, with nothing left to end it. S6 leaves a seat that never joined running with
nothing to do. S7 clears the debt without the connector's proof that the seat's launched
processes are gone. S8 stops a seat that never joined only after its spawn's terminal is
published, so a stalled publish leaves it running. S9 drops a deadline whose terminal write was
refused, and S10 leaves that seat running past its deadline. S11 settles a never-served task's
debt at the readiness verdict, before the seat's exit and its connector's proof.
S12 admits a Claude-style connector on a runtime that cannot report its startup outcome, so the
seat's task would be served on no evidence of channels. S13 and S14 move the turn-frame bound one
character each way, and S15 measures the task without the deadline line it can carry. S16 serves a
seat whose startup skipped the channel prompt, S17 serves it at its join before its notice, and
S18 serves a task whose spawn has no succeeded terminal, which a successor reads as never served. S19 names
a seat its failed startup watch stopped `seat-exited` when its exit lands before the launch reads the outcome.
